prerequisites: Knowledge from previous lectures in Mathematics, Physics, Electrical Engineering

learning_outcomes.text: Graduates have a thorough understanding of the system concept and can explain the analysis and synthesis of control loops using a unified systemic approach.
They can appropriately name suitable controllers for problems and apply dimensioning procedures.
Graduates understand simple requirements for control loops formulated from technical applications and can assign them to the control engineering toolkit.
The systemic approach of control engineering allows graduates to develop control approaches for various technical domains (electrical engineering, mechatronics, process engineering).

syllabus_topics: Basic concepts of control engineering (open-loop control, closed-loop control, application areas)
Description and analysis of linear systems in time and frequency domain
Requirements for the control loop, characteristic value-based design procedures, controller design in the frequency domain
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is a written exam. The ungraded assessment is experimental work, consisting of approximately 6 experiments each lasting 90 minutes. The duration of the written exam is specified in the valid study regulations.
bibliography: K. J. Astom, M. Murray: Feedback Systems: An Introduction for Scientists and Engineers. Princeton University Press. 2021.
M. Horn, N. Dourdoumas: Regelungstechnik. Pearson. 2004.
